name: Regents' and Chancellor's Scholarship
value: Honorary scholarship with a minimum award of $2,500 per year. Scholars with financial need receive grant and scholarship support up to their full need as assessed by the Financial Aid and Scholarships Office. Renewable for up to eight semesters for students entering from high school. Benefits also include priority class enrollment, faculty mentorship, guaranteed on-campus housing during the scholarship, and eligibility for up to $1,000 in research or professional development funding.
deadline: No separate application. Consideration comes from the UC application (the UC filing deadline is not listed on the scholarship page). Faculty interviews of first-year candidates take place in early March and decisions are sent at the end of March (displayed without a year).
apply: All students who apply to UC Berkeley are automatically considered. Candidates are selected from top applicants through holistic review by the Academic Senate Committee on Undergraduate Scholarships, Honors, and Financial Aid, and selected candidates are interviewed by faculty. File the FAFSA or CA Dream Act Application to be considered for the need-based portion.
eligibility: First-year applicants to UC Berkeley, including California residents, out-of-state students and international students (transfer students are also considered).
notes: The dollar amount beyond the $2,500 minimum depends on financial need. If you receive a need-based award, outside scholarships can reduce it.

name: Presidential Scholar Award
value: Full tuition, renewable annually with a 3.0 GPA and good academic standing. Not dependent on financial need. The award amount is based on tuition at the time it is set and is renewed at the same dollar amount.
deadline: Submit the application for admission by November 1, 2026. Priority Round: attend Senior Fall Visit Day on October 17, 2026 and complete a Presidential Scholar Interview there; notification by December 31, 2026. Standard Round: semi-finalists are notified by December 31, 2026, must complete a virtual interview by January 24, 2027, and are notified of award status by February 1, 2027.
apply: No separate scholarship application. Students are nominated to compete based on their admission materials, then complete a Presidential Scholar Interview.
eligibility: New entering domestic and international first-year students who apply for admission by November 1, 2026. Typically awarded to students with unweighted GPAs of 3.8 or higher in a rigorous curriculum and/or top 15% class rank (a typical profile, not a minimum).
notes: Wooster is test-optional and does not consider SAT or ACT scores for merit scholarships. Wooster is need-aware for international applicants. Wooster merit is capped at full tuition and applies only to tuition. The College Scholar award (also automatic, same November 1 deadline) is a lower tier.

name: Top Scholar Competition (Citrone, Madison and Davis awards)
value: Top Scholar awards added to an existing merit scholarship: Citrone Scholars Program (four-year full-tuition merit scholarships, number varies by year), Madison Scholarship (full tuition, fees, room and board for up to four years, one recipient), Davis Fellowship (full tuition for up to four years, awarded every other year to one student), Hurt Scholarship ($10,000, by invitation for Top Scholars interested in the sciences), and the Presidential Scholarship.
deadline: Competition dates for the fall 2027 entering class are not published on the scholarship page.
apply: All admission applicants are considered for merit scholarships with no separate form. Any student awarded the Birthplace Scholarship ($45,000 for 2026-27 entrants) is eligible to compete in the Top Scholar Competition.
eligibility: Admitted first-year applicants to Hampden-Sydney College (a men's college) who receive the Birthplace Scholarship.
notes: The merit amounts on the page are stated for students entering in 2026-27; fall 2027 amounts and competition dates are unconfirmed.

name: Presidential Scholarship and National Scholarship
value: Presidential Scholarship: $1,000 to $10,000 each year for four years. National Scholarship (non-residents): $2,500, $5,000, $10,000 or $15,000 each year for four years.
deadline: Full scholarship consideration requires a complete freshman application by the corresponding deadline: Early Action I November 1, Early Action II December 1, Regular January 1 (displayed without a year). Scholarship recipients are notified by March 31.
apply: No separate application. Admitted freshmen are considered based on a holistic review of the admission application.
eligibility: Admitted freshmen who are US citizens or permanent residents or eligible under the Minnesota Prosperity Act. The National Scholarship is for residents of any state except Minnesota, North Dakota, Wisconsin and Manitoba.
notes: Highly competitive; the university notes that demonstration of financial need is required for certain academic scholarships, but the Presidential and National Scholarships list no need criterion. ACT/SAT scores are not required for 2027 applicants. A limited number of scholarships exist for international students.

provider: Sewanee: The University of the South
name: Vice-Chancellor's and Benedict Scholarships
value: Vice-Chancellor's Scholarship: full tuition, fees, room and board annually (1 awarded). Benedict Scholarship: full tuition, fees, room and board annually (2 awarded). Renewable with satisfactory academic progress.
deadline: No separate scholarship deadline is listed. Consideration requires a complete Common Application and all required admission documents.
apply: Every applicant is considered for academic scholarships by submitting the Common Application and all required admission documents on the Applicant Status Page.
eligibility: First-year applicants to Sewanee.
notes: Only three of these top awards are given each year. Other automatic awards include the EQB Award ($5,000 to $34,000 annually) and the Wilkins Scholarship ($5,000 on top of the EQB Award).

name: New American University National Scholar Award
value: Arizona residents: $15,000 per year for National Merit Finalists ($60,000 over four years) or $10,000 per year for College Board National Recognition Program awardees ($40,000 over four years). Nonresidents: $17,500 per year for eight semesters ($70,000 over four years) for National Merit Finalists or National Recognition Program awardees who are admitted to and enroll in Barrett, The Honors College. Replaces any earlier New American University award.
deadline: National Merit Finalists must select ASU as their first-choice institution with the National Merit Scholarship Corporation by May 1 (displayed without a year).
apply: Apply to ASU, activate your ASURITE ID, and (for nonresidents) apply to and enroll in Barrett, The Honors College. Finalists must name ASU as first choice with NMSC.
eligibility: High school seniors named National Merit Finalists or College Board National Recognition Program awardees who are admitted to ASU.
notes: Qualifying depends on National Merit Finalist or National Recognition Program status. Nonresidents who do not enroll in Barrett keep their original New American University award instead.

name: Rensselaer Medal
value: $40,000 per year, guaranteed for four years (five years for the B.Arch. program), a total of $160,000, for each Medalist who is accepted and enrolls at Rensselaer.
deadline: High school nominations are due by May 1 of the student's junior year (displayed without a year). For current seniors, the nomination window was in spring of junior year.
apply: Students do not apply. Officials at each participating high school nominate one outstanding math and science student in the junior class through the secure medal website. Medalists who then apply to Rensselaer, are accepted and enroll receive the scholarship.
eligibility: High school juniors nominated by a participating high school for distinguished achievement in mathematics and science.
notes: Seniors who already received the Medal as juniors should apply to Rensselaer to use it. RPI gives only the single highest merit award a student qualifies for; awards are not combined.

name: Cincinnatus Presidential Scholarship
value: 20 Presidential Scholarships of $120,000 awarded annually (an estimated $30,000 per year covering full tuition, fees, room, board and a book allowance). Century and University Scholarships of $6,000 to $24,000 total are also awarded through Cincinnatus. A $3,000 annual Cincinnatus Out-of-State Scholarship is added for eligible nonresidents. Renewable with a 3.0 GPA and 30 hours of community service each year.
deadline: Submit a completed first-year application and required materials by November 1 of senior year (displayed without a year). Notifications begin in February and continue through mid-March.
apply: No separate scholarship application. Submit a complete Common Application (with fee or waiver and official transcript) by November 1; qualifying students are determined from the overall admission application.
eligibility: Incoming first-year students in all academic disciplines at the University of Cincinnati.
notes: ACT/SAT scores and a letter of recommendation are optional parts of the application.

name: Presidential Scholarship (nonresident)
value: $15,000 per year, renewable for four years (totaling $60,000) for newly admitted students. Paid each semester and can apply to all charges on the university bill.
deadline: Submit a completed application for admission no later than Jan. 15 (displayed without a year). Offers arrive with the admission decision.
apply: No separate application. Incoming nonresident first-year students are considered based on the materials in their admission application.
eligibility: Incoming nonresident first-year students who remain nonresidents for tuition purposes. Receiving an in-state tuition exception makes a student ineligible.
notes: Highly selective. ACT/SAT scores are not considered and will not be reviewed if submitted. There is no appeal process. Recipients cannot also receive the CU Boulder Chancellor's Achievement Scholarship. Must enroll full time (12+ credits) each fall and spring.

name: Schreyer Honors College Academic Excellence Scholarship
value: $5,275 annual scholarship for every incoming first-year Schreyer Scholar, renewable for all four years. Schreyer also offers additional grants for experiences such as study abroad and research.
deadline: November 15 at 11:59 PM EST (displayed without a year). Both the Penn State application and the Schreyer Honors College application, with all required documents, must be submitted by then.
apply: Apply to Penn State and submit the separate Schreyer Honors College application with the college's essay and short answer questions and two letters of recommendation.
eligibility: First-year applicants to Penn State who are admitted to the Schreyer Honors College.
notes: The scholarship comes with admission to Schreyer; admission to the honors college is the competitive step.

name: Regents Scholarship
value: All Regents Scholars are considered for a $2,000 honorarium regardless of financial need, supplemented by additional need-based aid for students with need. Entering freshmen receive a four-year scholarship (12 straight academic quarters).
deadline: Selected applicants are invited to submit a Regents Scholarship application at the beginning of February, before admission decisions are released (displayed without a year). The UC application deadline is not listed on the scholarship page.
apply: Apply to UCLA through the UC application. UCLA invites selected applicants to complete a separate Regents Scholarship application.
eligibility: Entering freshmen and transfer applicants to UCLA selected for an invitation.
notes: Only the $2,000 honorarium is independent of need; any larger amount depends on financial need. Scholars must keep a 3.0 GPA and enroll in at least 12 units each quarter.

name: Regents Scholarship
value: New Regents Scholars receive an honorarium award of $7,500, disbursed over three quarters. Scholars with demonstrated financial need may receive an additional stipend. The scholarship spans twelve quarters of undergraduate study for freshman recipients.
deadline: No separate application or deadline. Consideration is based on the UC application; the UC filing deadline is not listed on the scholarship page.
apply: All UC Davis applicants are considered solely on the information in the UC application. Selected admitted students are notified with their admission offer.
eligibility: Students entering UC Davis as freshmen (junior transfers and continuing students entering junior year are also eligible). Selection is based on academic achievements and personal accomplishments rather than financial need.
notes: The honorarium is merit-based; any stipend beyond it depends on financial need. Scholars must keep a 3.25 cumulative GPA, complete at least 39 units each year and stay full time.

name: Regents Scholarship for Entering Freshmen
value: $20,000 scholarship paid at $5,000 per year for four undergraduate years, plus first-choice UC San Diego college assignment (subject to availability), priority enrollment, a first-quarter research program (Regents Scholar Research Initiative, subject to availability) and a faculty mentor program.
deadline: File the UC Application for Admission and Scholarships by the Nov. 30 deadline (displayed without a year). Recipients are notified when College Financing Plans become available.
apply: No other paperwork. Filing the UC application is the only step.
eligibility: Entering freshmen (California residents and non-residents) who are US citizens, permanent residents, or California Dream Act students, with demonstrated academic excellence.

name: Chancellor's Scholarship for Entering First-Year
value: Honorarium of up to $5,000 per year for 4 undergraduate years (up to $20,000 total), plus guaranteed housing and priority enrollment. Grant awards are based on financial need.
deadline: File the UC Application for Admission and Scholarships by the Nov. 30 deadline, and the FAFSA by April 2 or the California Dream Act Application (displayed without a year). Recipients are notified in March with the admission notice.
apply: File the UC application; to establish financial need, file the FAFSA or the California Dream Act Application. No other paperwork.
eligibility: Entering first-year California residents who are US citizens, permanent residents, or California Dream Act students, with demonstrated academic excellence. Other factors include the personal statement, activities, first-generation status, and educational environment and economic background.
notes: Award amount is set by financial need.

name: Regents Scholarship
value: $5,000 per year for four years for entering freshmen, plus priority registration, four years of guaranteed housing, extended library borrowing, membership in the Regents Scholars Association and dedicated academic advising.
deadline: No separate application. Selection is based on the UC Application for Admission; students are notified in March if selected (displayed without a year).
apply: All freshmen admitted for fall are considered based on their UC application. No additional information is required.
eligibility: Admitted fall freshmen who are US citizens, permanent residents, or non-citizens qualifying under California Assembly Bills 130 or 131. UCSB typically offers the scholarship to students within the top two percent of admitted freshmen.
notes: Scholars must keep quarterly and cumulative GPAs of 3.20 and complete 12 units per quarter. The page currently notes that all 2026-27 awards have been made.

name: Regents' Scholarship
value: A monetary honorarium (amount not stated; final amount subject to federal and state financial aid regulations), renewable for three additional years for freshmen, plus four years of guaranteed on-campus housing and a transcript annotation.
deadline: No separate application. Recipients must submit the Statement of Intent to Register by the SIR deadline to accept.
apply: Scholars are selected from the UC application based on academic achievement and other qualifications, and receive a signed award letter through the applicant portal.
eligibility: Entering UCI students who are US citizens, eligible non-citizens, or students qualifying under AB130 or AB131. Students must be confirmed California residents to retain the scholarship.
notes: The honorarium amount is not published. Scholars must enroll in at least 12 units and keep a 3.25 cumulative GPA each quarter.

name: Provost Scholarship
value: Four-year scholarship covering tuition and fees up to $16,000 per year (maximum $8,000 per semester), an estimated total value of $64,000. The Deans' Scholarship (up to $8,000 per year) is awarded through the same review. Merit scholarships cover in-state costs only.
deadline: Common Application plus official high school transcript must be received by Nov. 1 (displayed without a year). Notification by the beginning of April.
apply: No separate application. All incoming first-year students who apply by Nov. 1 are considered for university-level scholarships.
eligibility: Incoming first-year VCU applicants. Recipients are selected on academic merit; leadership, community service and artistic talent may also be considered.
notes: Renewable for up to three more years with 28 credit hours per year and a 3.3 cumulative GPA. The FAFSA is encouraged but not stated as required.

name: Edward G. Rector Scholarship
value: Full-tuition scholarship plus access to exclusive programming, including networking with alumni. Renewable with a 3.0 cumulative GPA.
deadline: No scholarship deadline is listed on the merit awards page. Invitations are extended to eligible candidates during admission review.
apply: Apply for admission. Eligible candidates are invited to complete the Rector process, which includes a required essay.
eligibility: Top academic performers among DePauw applicants (typically the top 5% of applicants), selected on rigorous academic records and leadership.
notes: DePauw's other merit awards, including the Presidential Award of Excellence and DePauw Distinguished Scholarship, are automatic and range up to half the cost of attendance.

name: Trustee Scholarship Program (Trustee Fellows and Trustee Scholars)
value: 24 awards each year. The top eight recipients are Trustee Fellows and receive a full-ride award covering standard tuition and food and housing, plus faculty mentoring. The other 16 are Trustee Scholars and receive half tuition. Both are renewable for up to four years with a cumulative 3.40 QPA.
deadline: Submit the online admissions application and the Trustee Scholarship application by Nov. 1 (displayed without a year). Music majors must audition before Dec. 1. Finalists interview on campus in early December; recipients are notified in mid-January.
apply: Submit the Grove City College admissions application, then start the separate Trustee Scholarship application in the application portal. Finalists are invited to an on-campus interview.
eligibility: First-time freshmen applying to Grove City College. The college looks for strong academics, leadership, community service, cultural maturity, initiative and an entrepreneurial spirit.
notes: Grove City College does not accept federal financial aid. Trustee Scholars may also receive need-based aid up to the cost of education.

name: Frederick Douglass Distinguished Scholars Program
value: Full tuition, mandatory fees, U-Pass, books, on-campus housing and a meal plan, renewable for four years if academic requirements are met. About five scholars are admitted each year.
deadline: The application deadline for fall 2027 entry is not stated on the program pages.
apply: Separate program application; finalists take part in on-campus interviews. Contact the program at 202-885-6194 for current instructions.
eligibility: Incoming first-year students who are US citizens or permanent residents, within four years of high school graduation, who aspire to a graduate or professional degree, with a minimum 3.8 unweighted GPA (or 4.0 weighted). Historically underrepresented minority students and students from economically disadvantaged backgrounds are strongly encouraged to apply.
notes: Unconfirmed: the fall 2027 application deadline. The program describes itself as merit-based, selecting on scholastic achievement, leadership and interest in graduate or professional school.

name: Scott Scholars Program (Heider College of Business)
value: Full tuition, room and board, with business-focused programming and direct engagement with Omaha's business community. Creighton describes it as the university's top merit-based scholarship. Four years.
deadline: Dates for fall 2027 entry are not yet posted. For the previous cycle, the admission application and credentials were due December 1 and the program application was due January 10, 2026.
apply: Submit the application for undergraduate admission, then complete the Distinguished Scholars Program application (opens in November in the New Student Portal) and an interview. In-person interviews at Distinguished Scholars Interview Day are encouraged; virtual interviews are available.
eligibility: Incoming first-year students planning to study in the Heider College of Business.
notes: Unconfirmed: the fall 2027 program application deadline. Creighton's Harper Nursing Scholars Program ($40,000 annual scholarship for seven to eight students each year) runs through the same Distinguished Scholars process.

name: Premier Scholarship Program (JGK III, Moore, William T. Young, Kenan)
value: JGK III Scholarship: full tuition, fees, on-campus housing and meals. Jennifer A. Moore Endowed Scholarship: full tuition, fees, on-campus housing and meals. William T. Young Scholarship: full tuition and fees. Kenan Scholarship: amounts begin at $36,000 per year.
deadline: Students chosen to compete must apply by December 1 (Early Action Deadline #2) (displayed without a year).
apply: Apply for admission. Students are selected to compete based on the application, essay, transcript, resume or activity list, letters of recommendation and test scores if provided, and receive further instructions.
eligibility: First-year applicants to Transylvania University selected to compete for Premier Scholarships.
notes: Premier awards cannot be combined with other merit scholarships beyond Transylvania's standard tuition and fees.

name: Sullivan Scholars Program
value: Two full scholarships each year covering tuition, housing and meals, with mentoring and preparation for postgraduate awards such as Fulbright and Rhodes.
deadline: Submit the Common Application to Seattle University by January 15. Invited students receive the supplementary application in January (available by late November); the Sullivan Scholars application is due March 1 (displayed without a year).
apply: Apply to Seattle University. Eligible admitted applicants are invited to complete a supplementary Sullivan application in the Redhawk Admissions Portal. No campus visit is required.
eligibility: Students enrolled at a Catholic or Jesuit high school anywhere in the world. Most selected scholars have a cumulative unweighted GPA of 3.7 or higher with challenging coursework plus leadership and service (a typical profile).
notes: Limited to students at Catholic or Jesuit high schools. The former on-campus Sullivan Leadership Award competition ended in 2024.

name: Regents Scholars Program
value: $40,000 to $45,000 annually, renewable up to 4 years. Pepperdine's most competitive merit scholarship.
deadline: No separate deadline is listed; consideration comes from the admission application with SAT, ACT or CLT scores submitted.
apply: No separate application. All applicants who submit SAT/ACT/CLT scores are considered; students in the top 8% to 10% of the admitted first-year class are invited into the program.
eligibility: First-year (and transfer) applicants to Pepperdine's Seaver College who submit SAT, ACT or CLT scores. Evaluation is based on unweighted recalculated GPA and test scores.
notes: Pepperdine is test optional for admission, but test scores are required for Regents consideration. Not stackable with the George Pepperdine Achievement Award.

name: Archer Presidential Scholarship and William Randolph Hearst Endowed Scholarship
value: Archer Presidential Scholarship: full tuition, room, board, books and fees for about five first-year students, renewable for up to four years (eight semesters; five years for B.Arch.). Hearst Endowed Scholarship: one scholarship covering full tuition, room, board, books and fees.
deadline: Complete the admission application by the Early Action I deadline of November 1 (displayed without a year). Finalists are notified in late November or early December and interview on campus in late January. Recipients must pay the enrollment deposit by April 1.
apply: No additional steps at the initial stage. Candidates who first qualify for the Trustee Scholarship (currently $25,000) are considered; 12 to 15 finalists are invited to interview for the Archer award and about five for the Hearst award.
eligibility: First-year applicants to Belmont. These awards recognize about the top 1% of first-year applicants; a strong candidate typically has a cumulative GPA above 4.43 and an ACT of 34 or SAT of 1430 if a score is submitted (a typical profile, not a minimum).
notes: Belmont states that demonstrated financial need may be considered for the Archer award, so filing the FAFSA is highly encouraged for those selected.

name: Thomas A. Dingledine Scholarship
value: In combination with other JMU scholarships, equivalent to in-state tuition and fees per year for four years. Up to 10 awarded each year.
deadline: Submit the JMU Early Action application with the Honors College section by November 1, and the Dingledine application in the Madison Scholarships Hub by November 15 (displayed without a year). Finalists interview January to February; recipients are notified in late February.
apply: Apply Early Action with the Honors College section, then complete the General Scholarship Application and the Dingledine application in the Madison Scholarships Hub: two 250-word essays, unofficial transcript with senior schedule, and lists of activities and awards.
eligibility: Incoming first-year students applying to the JMU Honors College through Early Action who have either a 3.6 cumulative unweighted GPA (or 89 on a 100-point scale) or a 1250 SAT / 27 ACT (official scores received by November 1).
notes: Recipients must stay in the Honors College, join a leadership and service community with a one-credit seminar each semester, and keep a 3.0 GPA. Cannot be combined with several other JMU merit awards.

name: Park Scholar Program
value: Full tuition and room and board at Ithaca College for all four years, as long as scholars maintain high grades and a consistent record of service and leadership. Awarded regardless of financial need. About 4 to 5 awards are likely each year.
deadline: Complete the Common Application (recommended no later than November 15, 2026), then the Park Scholar application in IC Connect by December 1, 2026. Finalists notified by January 25, 2027; Finalist Weekend over Zoom February 6-8, 2027; recipients notified at the end of February.
apply: Apply to Ithaca College with a preferred major in the Roy H. Park School of Communications, then submit the Park Scholar application in IC Connect: three essays, two additional recommendation letters (from people who did not write for the Common App) and a personal history or resume. Finalists take part in individual and group interviews.
eligibility: US citizens or eligible non-citizens applying as first-year students to an undergraduate major in the Roy H. Park School of Communications. Transfer students are not eligible. No minimum GPA or test score is set.
notes: Roughly 300 to 400 students apply each year.

name: Presidential Scholarship
value: Annual full-tuition-and-fees scholarship, renewable for up to 4 years (8 semesters) with full-time enrollment and satisfactory progress. Replaces any other Ithaca College Scholarship and cannot be combined with a scholar program.
deadline: Presidential Scholarship application due by November 1 (displayed without a year). US citizens and eligible FAFSA filers must also submit the FAFSA by November 1; international students submit the Ithaca College Financial Aid application by November 1.
apply: Apply to Ithaca College, then complete the additional Presidential Scholarship application online.
eligibility: Select first-year Ithaca College students who embody the college's values of academic excellence, respect and accountability, innovation, sustainability, and equity. International students may apply.
notes: A FAFSA (or the college's financial aid application for international students) is required to receive the award; the page does not say whether need affects selection.

name: General John J. Pershing Scholarship and President John R. Kirk Scholarship
value: Pershing Scholarship (about twelve awards annually): full-time tuition and the average cost of room and board, plus a one-time $4,000 study abroad stipend. Kirk Scholarship: $23,000 for out-of-state students and $17,000 for in-state students. Both supersede other Truman-funded awards and are renewable under Truman's renewal guidelines.
deadline: Application with ACT/SAT score, essay and activities resume must be complete prior to Dec. 1 (displayed without a year). Competitive selections occur December through early February.
apply: No separate scholarship application. Submit the admission application with an ACT or SAT score, the admission essay and an activities resume before December 1.
eligibility: First-year applicants to Truman State. Top candidates typically rank in the top 3% of their high school class with ACT or SAT scores in the top 3% nationally (a typical profile).
notes: An ACT or SAT score is part of the required file for these competitive awards.

provider: University of Texas at San Antonio
name: UT San Antonio Top Scholar Program
value: Premier Honors College scholar program with signature enrichment programming, research access, faculty mentoring and a living-learning community. The current program pages do not state the scholarship dollar amount.
deadline: The application period is September 1 to December 1 of senior year; the Top Scholar application deadline is December 1 (displayed without a year).
apply: Apply to UT San Antonio through ApplyTexas or the Common App, get a myUTSA ID, complete the General Scholarship Application in the Scholarship Hub, then submit the Top Scholar application and make sure your reference is complete. Selected finalists are invited for a selection interview.
eligibility: First-time college students. The program says students with the best chance of an interview invitation have a 1440+ SAT or 32+ ACT (scores optional), top 5% class rank, community volunteerism and school leadership, and Texas residency. All majors are welcome.
notes: Unconfirmed: the award value for the fall 2027 cohort. Scholars must keep a 3.50 GPA, live on campus and complete 30 hours per year.

name: College Merit Scholars Programs (Engineering, Malesardi Arts and Sciences, Management)
value: $40,000 annual scholarship, renewable for up to eight fall/spring semesters while program requirements are met. Offered separately in the College of Engineering (Engineering Merit Scholars), the College of Arts and Sciences (Malesardi Arts and Sciences Merit Scholarship) and the Freeman College of Management (Management Merit Scholars).
deadline: Consideration follows your admission round: Early Decision I Nov. 1; Early Decision II and Regular Decision Jan. 10 (displayed without a year). Notifications generally come with admission decisions.
apply: No separate scholarship application is required for these programs; apply for admission to Bucknell.
eligibility: High-achieving, intellectually curious incoming first-year students admitted to the relevant college.
notes: Bucknell states that most merit funding is awarded to students with demonstrated institutional need, with a limited amount for students without need or who do not apply for aid. Students cannot receive multiple academic scholarships. These programs replace the Presidential Fellowship for new students.

name: Weissman Scholarship
value: Four-year, full-tuition scholarship plus financial support for scholars to develop their talents and pursue personal passions, with retreats, tailored study abroad and program trips. Renewable with a 3.3 cumulative GPA.
deadline: Early Decision I or Early Action applicants: scholarship essay due December 1, 2026 (notification by mid-January). Early Decision II or Regular Decision applicants: essay due February 1, 2027 (notification by mid-March).
apply: Apply for admission to Babson, then submit a scholarship essay (650 words maximum) or a 2-minute video, not both, through the applicant portal.
eligibility: First-year applicants only. Selection is based on academic excellence and intellectual passion, distinction in leadership, and a vision for how the Weissman program would support their goals.

name: Arthur M. Blank School for Entrepreneurial Leadership Scholarship
value: Four-year, full-tuition, merit-based award.
deadline: Early Decision I or Early Action applicants: scholarship essay due December 1, 2026 (notification by mid-January). Early Decision II or Regular Decision applicants: essay due February 1, 2027 (notification by mid-March).
apply: Apply for admission to Babson, then submit a 650-word essay or a 2-minute video (not both) through the applicant portal describing a time you embodied one or two of Arthur Blank's core values to effect change.
eligibility: Undergraduate applicants to Babson. Selection is based on academic excellence, distinction in leadership, commitment to Mr. Blank's six core values and an entrepreneurial leadership mindset.

name: Regents Scholar Tuition Commitment
value: Full University of Nebraska-Lincoln undergraduate tuition for up to 120 credit hours or completion of a bachelor's degree, including summers and differential tuition. Combined non-loan aid cannot exceed cost of attendance.
deadline: Priority: November 1. Final: February 1 (displayed without a year). Final official scores from the February test date or earlier must arrive by May 1.
apply: Apply for admission to UNL and send official ACT or SAT scores.
eligibility: Admitted first-year Nebraska residents with a minimum composite ACT of 32 (or SAT equivalent; superscores excluded) who show academic distinction. Recipients must be US citizens or qualified aliens lawfully present in the US.
notes: Renewal requires a 3.500 cumulative GPA or upper-25% class rank each year.

name: Chancellor's Tuition Scholarship (Out-of-State)
value: Full non-resident portion of tuition plus $4,000 per year for up to four years. National Merit Scholars may qualify for an additional $500 stipend.
deadline: Priority: November 1. Out-of-State: May 1 (displayed without a year).
apply: Apply for admission to UNL. National Merit Finalists must select UNL as their first-choice school with the National Merit Scholarship Corporation.
eligibility: Out-of-state first-year students of academic distinction who are finalists in nationally recognized scholar competitions such as National Merit or the College Board National Recognition Programs. National Recognition awardees must have at least a 28 ACT (or SAT equivalent) and a 3.500 GPA. Recipients must be US citizens or qualified aliens lawfully present in the US.
notes: Renewal requires a 3.500 cumulative GPA and 24 hours per year. Not transferable to other University of Nebraska campuses.

name: Oberlin Midwest Merit Scholarship
value: $25,000 each year, a total of $100,000 over four years (five years for Double Degree students). Renewable for 8 semesters (10 for Double Degree or BA+BFA students) with full-time enrollment.
deadline: No separate deadline; awarded to admitted students who enroll.
apply: No separate application. Oberlin reviews all admitted students for merit scholarships automatically.
eligibility: All admitted, newly enrolling students from Ohio, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, North Dakota, South Dakota and Wisconsin.
notes: Limited to students from the 12 listed Midwestern states. Oberlin also awards a $10,000 Oberlin Commitment Scholarship to all enrolling students and John F. Oberlin Scholarships for academic achievement in the College of Arts and Sciences.

name: Lilly Awards
value: Tuition, standard fees, on-campus housing and food each year; more than $240,000 over four years.
deadline: Apply for admission and submit the Lilly Award application by January 3, 2027. Finalists are interviewed February 21-22, 2027.
apply: Apply for admission to Wabash and submit the separate Lilly Award application (read it carefully for all requirements). Finalists are interviewed.
eligibility: Applicants to Wabash College (a men's college) who meet at least one of: a 3.5 GPA (4.0 scale), top 10 percent class rank, or an SAT of at least 1240 (EBRW + Math) or ACT composite of 26. Selection is based on character, creativity and academic accomplishment.

name: Honors Scholarships (Scarlet Honors Weekend)
value: $3,000 scholarship guaranteed (renewable for 4 years) with the possibility of up to a full-tuition scholarship.
deadline: Apply for admission by December 1, 2026, and attend Scarlet Honors Weekend on December 4-5, 2026 or February 21-22, 2027.
apply: Apply for admission to Wabash by December 1, 2026 and attend one of the Scarlet Honors Weekend sessions, where the honors scholarship competition takes place.
eligibility: First-year applicants to Wabash College (a men's college).

name: Michael R. Lovell Presidential Scholarship
value: Full ride covering tuition, fees, housing and food, renewable for four years (eight semesters) with good academic standing and program requirements. Up to 4 awards, with a designated faculty mentor and co-curricular programming.
deadline: February 1 (displayed without a year).
apply: Apply and be accepted to Marquette first. Admitted students then receive instructions on their student status page for submitting the additional scholarship materials.
eligibility: Students admitted to Marquette with demonstrated commitment to social justice and community through volunteerism, engagement and leadership, and academic excellence (a preferred minimum 3.8 GPA). Test-optional applicants receive equal consideration.
notes: The 3.8 GPA is described as preferred, not required.

name: Ignatian Scholarship
value: Invite-only full-tuition scholarship awarded in the freshman year, renewable under Loyola's Scholarship Renewal Policy.
deadline: Not published for fall 2027 entry. Candidates interview in person with faculty and administrators in late March (displayed without a year).
apply: By invitation only. Invited candidates must take part in an in-person interview.
eligibility: Admitted first-year students invited by Loyola.
notes: Unconfirmed: the current scholarship page describes awards for students entering Fall 2026; fall 2027 terms and invitation timing are not yet posted.

name: Academic Merit Scholarships (Kenyon Excellence, Kenyon Honors, President's, Distinguished Academic)
value: Merit scholarships currently ranging from $15,000 to $35,000 a year, renewable all four years with satisfactory academic progress. Talent scholarships in studio art, music and writing ($25,000 per year) require separate applications.
deadline: No separate deadline for academic merit; recipients are notified with their admission decision.
apply: No additional application. All first-year applicants are considered without regard to financial need.
eligibility: All first-year applicants to Kenyon College. Awards recognize academic excellence and meaningful involvement in school or community activities.
notes: Students eligible for both talent and merit scholarships receive an enhanced award greater than the highest individual value.

name: Green and Gold Presidential Waiver Award (non-Florida residents)
value: For the most recent posted cycle: about $44,000 (up to $11,000 per year) as an out-of-state tuition waiver. Lower tiers: Green and Gold Directors Waiver (~$36,000) and Green and Gold Scholars Waiver (~$20,000).
deadline: Not yet posted for fall 2027. For Summer or Fall 2026, the complete freshman application was due January 15, 2026.
apply: No separate application. Admitted first-time-in-college students are automatically considered when their complete application (application, test scores, STARS or transcript, fee) is in by the scholarship deadline.
eligibility: Admitted first-time-in-college students who are not Florida residents.
notes: Unconfirmed: fall 2027 amounts and deadline. The waiver is canceled if residency changes to in-state and cannot be combined with other tuition waivers.

name: Freshman Provost Award
value: One of UCF's most prestigious merit scholarships, with priority consideration for The Burnett Honors College (on completing the honors application). The award amount is not stated on UCF's pages.
deadline: A complete application for admission, including fee or waiver, SPARK Form and official SAT, ACT or CLT scores, must be received by the Early Action deadlines of Oct. 15 and Nov. 15 (displayed without a year) for merit consideration.
apply: No separate application. Students who apply for summer or fall admission are automatically considered.
eligibility: Florida residents entering as freshmen with outstanding academic credentials. Awarded to less than 10 percent of the entering freshman class.
notes: Unconfirmed: the dollar amount. Official test scores are required for merit consideration. Recipients must enroll in at least 12 UCF credit hours each fall and spring.

name: Spirit of Auburn Presidential Excellence Award (Alabama residents)
value: For fall 2026 entrants: full resident tuition and mandatory student services fees ($13,572 for 2026-27). Lower resident tiers in the same chart: Spirit of Auburn Presidential Scholarship ($11,500), Founders Scholarship ($9,000) and University Scholarship ($5,000).
deadline: Fall 2027 terms are not yet posted. Fall 2026 awards went to residents accepted as early action.
apply: Competitive merit is awarded through admission; see Auburn's first-year scholarship instructions for the current cycle.
eligibility: Alabama residents admitted to Auburn. The fall 2026 chart lists a minimum 4.0 high school GPA and a 35-36 ACT (or equivalent SAT) for the Presidential Excellence Award.
notes: Unconfirmed: fall 2027 criteria and amounts. Auburn says the chart is a guide, not a guarantee; each entering class competes with itself and awards depend on funding.

name: National Merit Finalist Package
value: Value of tuition for up to five years or 10 semesters (undergraduate and graduate or law studies); four years of on-campus housing at the regular room rate; $4,000 per year undergraduate supplemental scholarship for four years (a portion paid by NMSC); $2,000 one-time allowance for research or international study after one year at UA.
deadline: Admission application and supporting documents by the December 4 priority deadline (later applicants through May 1 considered on a space-available basis). List UA as college of choice with NMSC before May 1, 2027.
apply: Be named a National Merit Finalist, apply to UA by the December 4 priority deadline, and list The University of Alabama as your college of choice with NMSC before May 1, 2027.
eligibility: National Merit Finalists with a 3.5 or higher GPA after junior year. NMSC requires entrants to be US citizens or US lawful permanent residents intending to become citizens.
notes: Terms are for students naming UA before May 1, 2027 (fall 2027 entry). Admitted National Merit Semifinalists with a 3.5+ GPA are automatically eligible for the Presidential Scholarship instead of this package. Separate from UA's automatic out-of-state merit table.

name: National Merit Scholarship package
value: Out-of-state National Merit Finalists: competitive National Merit Scholarship package valued at more than $25,000 per year for four years. Florida residents who become Finalists: Benacquisto Scholarship plus Florida Bright Futures. Finalists can also get guaranteed admission to The Burnett Honors College (with application) and guaranteed on-campus housing.
deadline: Designate UCF as first choice with NMSC by the May 31 deadline.
apply: Be named a National Merit Semifinalist (considered for a scholarship upon admission), then advance to Finalist and designate UCF as your first choice with NMSC by May 31 for an increased award.
eligibility: Admitted National Merit Semifinalists and Finalists. NMSC requires entrants to be US citizens or US lawful permanent residents intending to become citizens.
notes: The page does not name an entry year and still links a 2025 newsletter; confirm fall 2027 values with UCF. Awards cover up to 8 fall and spring terms.

name: National Merit Scholar package
value: Florida residents: State of Florida Benacquisto Scholarship covering 100% of cost of attendance in fall and spring (reduced by Bright Futures and any NMSC award), plus USF National Merit Tradition of Excellence Award ($20,000; $5,000 per year) and a $2,000 Passport study abroad scholarship. Non-Florida residents: USF Golden Achievement Program scholarship covering 100% of cost of attendance in fall and spring (reduced by any NMSC award), plus the $2,000 Passport Scholarship.
deadline: Designate USF as first choice with NMSC by the May 31 deadline.
apply: Apply to USF, become a National Merit Finalist, and designate USF as your first-choice school with NMSC by May 31.
eligibility: High school graduates who are National Merit Finalists and selected USF as first choice with NMSC. Residency as determined by USF. NMSC requires entrants to be US citizens or US lawful permanent residents intending to become citizens.
notes: The page does not name an entry year (its linked National Merit guide is labeled 2026). These awards replace other Office of Admissions awards (Florida residents keep the Tradition of Excellence award). Semifinalists are considered for scholarships upon admission.

name: National Merit Finalist Scholarship
value: Fall 2026 package. Non-residents: total $153,450 (non-resident tuition waiver $90,600; resident tuition waiver $26,850; OU cash $22,000 at $5,500 per year; National Merit cash stipend $5,000; first-year housing scholarship $6,000; First-Year Associates $1,000; research and study abroad stipend $2,000). Residents: total $146,850. Tuition waiver can extend to five years.
deadline: For fall 2026: apply to OU by December 15, 2025 and name OU with NMSC by April 30, 2026. Fall 2027 dates not yet posted.
apply: Be a National Merit Finalist, apply to OU by its scholarship deadline, and name OU as first choice with NMSC by the NMSC deadline.
eligibility: Admitted National Merit Finalists entering OU. NMSC requires entrants to be US citizens or US lawful permanent residents intending to become citizens.
notes: Page shows only the fall 2026 package (updated December 2025). Does not cover full cost of attendance. Full-time enrollment and 24 OU hours per year required; GPA rules vary by component.

name: National Merit Scholars package
value: 2027-2028 estimates. Out-of-state: OSU Merit Scholarship up to $7,200 per year for four years; tuition scholarship $21,930 per year for up to five years (estimated); National Merit cash scholarship $2,000 per year for up to four years (estimated); College Dean's Award $2,000 per year for up to four years; total up to $154,500. In-state: OSRHE Rising Scholars Award up to $24,000 per year for four years; tuition scholarship $5,673 per year for up to five years; National Merit cash $2,000 per year; Dean's Award $2,000 per year; total up to $140,400.
deadline: Name OSU as first choice with NMSC by the NMSC deadline (date not stated on the page).
apply: Be a National Merit Finalist and name Oklahoma State University as your first choice with NMSC.
eligibility: National Merit Finalists enrolling full time at OSU. NMSC requires entrants to be US citizens or US lawful permanent residents intending to become citizens.
notes: Renewal: 3.25 GPA for the merit scholarship (in-state Rising Scholars too), 2.0 for the tuition scholarship, and 24 hours earned by the end of each spring.

name: National Merit Scholars Program package
value: Fall 2026 package: UT Dallas tuition for up to eight semesters; first-year housing (University Commons) or a 4x2 University Village apartment; COMET 14 meal plan or equivalent for on-campus scholars; book and supplies stipend; study abroad stipend; one-time summer research stipend; admission to the Collegium V Honors program.
deadline: Complete admissions application by the December 1 deadline; list UT Dallas as first choice with NMSC before the NMSC deadline.
apply: Be a National Merit Finalist, submit a complete UT Dallas application by December 1, be admitted, and list UT Dallas as first choice in the NMSC portal.
eligibility: Admitted National Merit Finalists. NMSC requires entrants to be US citizens or US lawful permanent residents intending to become citizens.
notes: Page shows the fall 2026 package; fall 2027 terms not yet posted. Research stipend requires an SSN.

name: National Merit Finalist Scholarship Package
value: Fall 2026 package: National Merit Finalist Scholarship $48,000 over four years ($12,000 per year); Housing Award approximately $33,824 over four years ($8,456 per year); non-residents also receive a tuition scholarship covering 100% of the non-resident portion of tuition.
deadline: Select MSU as first choice with NMSC (date not stated on the page).
apply: Be a National Merit Finalist, have a 9th to 11th grade GPA of 3.0+, and select MSU as first choice with NMSC.
eligibility: Entering first-time freshmen (Starkville) who are National Merit Finalists with a 3.0+ high school GPA. NMSC requires entrants to be US citizens or US lawful permanent residents intending to become citizens.
notes: Page lists the fall 2026 entry term. Housing award requires continuous on-campus residency. Cannot be combined with MSU's automatic freshman academic scholarships. MSU also has a separate National Merit Semifinalist package.

name: National Recognition Program Scholarship
value: Fall 2026: $40,000 over four years ($10,000 per year), plus possible additional coverage of non-resident tuition for eligible students. Renewable for up to 8 semesters.
deadline: Fall 2026 priority deadline was December 1, 2025; fall 2027 date not yet posted.
apply: Submit your College Board National Recognition Program certificate and apply to MSU by the priority deadline.
eligibility: Entering first-time freshmen with a College Board National Recognition Program award (African American, Hispanic, Indigenous or Rural/Small Town) and a 9th to 11th grade GPA of 3.0+.
notes: Page shows the fall 2026 term. Renewal: 3.0 college GPA and continuous full-time enrollment.

name: National Merit Scholarship (UF-sponsored)
value: $500 per year National Merit Scholarship from UF. Florida residents who receive it also qualify for the state Benacquisto Scholarship, which covers remaining cost of attendance after Bright Futures and the National Merit award.
deadline: Indicate UF as first choice with NMSC by May 31.
apply: Be a National Merit Finalist and list UF as first choice with NMSC by May 31.
eligibility: National Merit Finalists enrolling at UF. Benacquisto is for Florida residents. NMSC requires entrants to be US citizens or US lawful permanent residents intending to become citizens.
notes: The page does not name an entry year. The UF award itself is small; the large value comes from the state Benacquisto Scholarship for Florida residents.

name: National Merit Finalist / Benacquisto and Out-of-State National Merit Award
value: Florida residents: Benacquisto Scholarship equal to the full in-state cost of attendance minus Bright Futures and any National Merit award (disbursement $16,000 to $25,000 per year). Out-of-state: package with a total value of approximately $91,808 over four years, including a 100% out-of-state tuition waiver, a $16,000 Vires scholarship and a $2,000 NMSC stipend (if college-sponsored). All Finalists who apply to UROP in the first year are guaranteed admission to it.
deadline: List FSU as first choice with NMSC by May 1 of senior year.
apply: Be a National Merit Finalist awarded a National Merit, corporate or college-sponsored National Merit Scholarship, and list FSU as first choice with NMSC by May 1.
eligibility: National Merit Finalists graduating with a standard high school diploma. NMSC requires entrants to be US citizens or US lawful permanent residents intending to become citizens.
notes: The page does not name an entry year; the Vires amount is footnoted for admitted first-year students starting fall 2024 and later. Separate from FSU's Presidential Scholars and Stamps programs.

name: Academic Excellence National Merit and National Merit Finalist scholarships
value: 2026-2027 non-resident table: Academic Excellence National Merit Finalist/Semifinalist Scholarship covers full tuition, the standard cost of a double occupancy room and the full non-resident fee; plus National Merit Finalist Scholarship $4,000 ($1,000 per year) for Finalists who choose Ole Miss first. Mississippi residents (2025-2026 page): Academic Excellence award (full tuition and standard double room), $4,000 National Merit Finalist Award, and Barnard Scholarship $20,000 ($5,000 per year) for Finalists with a 3.0+ GPA.
deadline: Follows the National Merit announcement timeline.
apply: Be a National Merit Semifinalist or Finalist with a 3.0+ GPA; Finalists select Ole Miss as first choice with NMSC for the Finalist award.
eligibility: Entering freshmen with National Merit Semifinalist or Finalist status and a 3.0 or higher GPA. The $4,000 Finalist award excludes students receiving a National Merit corporate award. NMSC requires entrants to be US citizens or US lawful permanent residents intending to become citizens.
notes: Pages show 2026-2027 (non-resident) and 2025-2026 (resident) tables; fall 2027 terms not yet posted. Does not stack with Ole Miss's non-resident Academic Merit awards.

name: National Merit Semifinalist Package
value: For National Merit Semifinalists entering in fall 2027: full tuition (excluding summers) for four years and basic housing (upgrades at the student's cost), plus the NMSC National Merit Finalist Scholarship (minimum $750, if eligible).
deadline: By Nov. 1: submit all admission materials, complete an official campus visit, attend an on-campus in-person Semifinalist interview, and send two recommendation letters. Submit the Intent to Enroll form by May 1.
apply: Be a National Merit Semifinalist, complete the application, campus visit, in-person interview and two letters (one academic, one non-academic) by Nov. 1, designate Tulsa as first choice with NMSC by the final deadline, and commit by May 1.
eligibility: National Merit Semifinalists with a minimum weighted GPA of 4.0 (on a 4.0 scale). NMSC requires entrants to be US citizens or US lawful permanent residents intending to become citizens.
notes: Requires an in-person interview and campus visit. Minimum 12 credit hours per semester required.

name: National Merit Scholarship
value: Unlimited awards paying tuition, fees, on-campus housing and meals for four years.
deadline: Apply for admission according to National Merit deadlines.
apply: Be admitted as an incoming freshman, be a National Merit Finalist, and list Louisiana Tech as first choice with NMSC.
eligibility: Admitted incoming freshmen who are National Merit Finalists with a 3.0 cumulative GPA (4.0 unweighted scale). NMSC requires entrants to be US citizens or US lawful permanent residents intending to become citizens.
notes: The page does not name an entry year. Renewal: full-time enrollment and a 3.0 cumulative GPA.

name: National Merit Scholarship
value: 2026-27: approximately $22,000 per year for Idaho residents covering basic registration fees/tuition and the university-defined room and board; non-residents also receive a full non-resident tuition waiver (about $20,000). Over $85,000 in cash scholarships over four years plus the waiver for non-residents.
deadline: Declare Idaho as first choice with NMSC by its May 31 deadline.
apply: Be admitted as a first-year student directly from high school or home school, become a National Merit Finalist, send the Finalist letter to the Financial Aid Office, and name Idaho first choice with NMSC by May 31.
eligibility: First-year National Merit Finalists entering directly from high school or home school. NMSC requires entrants to be US citizens or US lawful permanent residents intending to become citizens.
notes: Page states 2026-27 values. Covers fall and spring only; students pay course fees and any housing cost above the university-defined amount.

name: National Merit Finalist scholarship
value: A competitive merit-based award for admitted National Merit Finalists; amount not stated on the page.
deadline: Fall 2026 cycle: priority deadline April 9, 2026 to designate Northeastern (for notice before May 1); designations after that and before August 1 remain eligible. Fall 2027 dates not yet posted.
apply: Be admitted to Northeastern and designate Northeastern University-Boston as your college choice with NMSC.
eligibility: Admitted National Merit Finalists. NMSC requires entrants to be US citizens or US lawful permanent residents intending to become citizens.
notes: Dates shown are for the fall 2026 cycle. This award may replace existing Northeastern merit awards.

name: National Merit Scholarship (Honors College)
value: Tuition and required fees, plus a $1,000 undergraduate research stipend and a $2,000 study abroad stipend.
deadline: Follow NMSC rules and deadlines for first-choice selection.
apply: Be a National Merit Finalist and select the University of Houston as your first-choice institution with NMSC.
eligibility: National Merit Finalists enrolling at UH. NMSC requires entrants to be US citizens or US lawful permanent residents intending to become citizens.
notes: The page does not name an entry year. UH adjusts its contribution if you receive an NMSC or corporate-sponsored award. FAFSA filers may qualify for more aid.

name: National Merit Scholars Program
value: Covers 100% of the approved cost of attendance for four years; the admissions page shows an annual total of $29,086 (tuition and fees $11,852 for 30 hours, housing $7,032, meals $4,280, books $1,200, transportation $2,731, miscellaneous $2,000), labeled 2024-2025. Includes automatic admission to the Honors College.
deadline: Admissions page: declare Texas Tech as college of choice by April 1. The scholarships office page still shows a May 31, 2022 date.
apply: Be a National Merit Finalist and designate Texas Tech as first choice with NMSC.
eligibility: National Merit Finalists, including non-residents. NMSC requires entrants to be US citizens or US lawful permanent residents intending to become citizens.
notes: Official pages show 2024-2025 figures and older deadlines; confirm fall 2027 terms. Aid is made up of federal, state and institutional gift aid (no loans). Renewal: 3.5 GPA and 30 hours per year.

name: Provost Scholars Award (National Merit Finalists)
value: $6,000 per year ($24,000 over four years).
deadline: List USC as first choice with NMSC by the stated NMSC deadline.
apply: Be a National Merit Finalist and list the University of South Carolina as your first choice with NMSC.
eligibility: Eligible National Merit Finalists. NMSC requires entrants to be US citizens or US lawful permanent residents intending to become citizens.
notes: The page does not name an entry year. Unlike other USC merit awards, it can be combined with any other university merit scholarship.

name: National Merit and National Recognition Program scholarships
value: National Merit Finalists: $4,000 per year. National Recognition Program Scholars: $2,500 per year. Students receive only one of these, at the highest amount.
deadline: NMSC sends Finalist rosters to UAB beginning in early March; no separate date stated.
apply: National Merit Finalists: name UAB first choice with NMSC. National Recognition Program Scholars: apply in BSMART and complete the National Scholarship Questions section with your notification letter and certificate.
eligibility: In-state and out-of-state students who are National Merit Finalists or College Board National Recognition Program Scholars.
notes: Page displays the 2026-2027 cycle. Stackable on UAB admissions merit scholarships.

name: National Merit UAH Platinum Scholarship
value: Full tuition (up to 18 credit hours per semester) for eight semesters; one year of on-campus housing at the regular room rate; course fees up to $500 per year; one-time $3,000 UAH-led summer study abroad allowance.
deadline: Be admitted to UAH and list UAH as college choice with NMSC by May 31.
apply: Be a National Merit Finalist, be admitted to UAH before May 31, and list UAH as your college choice with NMSC by May 31.
eligibility: National Merit Finalists admitted to UAH. NMSC requires entrants to be US citizens or US lawful permanent residents intending to become citizens.
notes: The page does not name an entry year.

name: National Merit Semifinalist and Finalist packages
value: For 2027 high school graduates. Semifinalist: full tuition for four years, plus campus housing, meal plan and a one-time $500 educational allowance for the freshman year only. Finalist: full tuition for four years, campus housing, meal plan and a $1,000 educational allowance for four years, plus a one-time $4,000 study abroad scholarship.
deadline: Semifinalists: be admitted by the March 1 priority deadline and accept the award in the GO System by May 1. Finalists: apply with official documentation in the GO System by May 1 and accept by July 1.
apply: Semifinalists need no separate application but must be admitted by March 1. Finalists apply in the Golden Opportunities (GO) system by May 1 and list USM as first choice with NMSC.
eligibility: First-year, full-time incoming freshmen (2027 high school graduates) named National Merit Semifinalists or Finalists. NMSC requires entrants to be US citizens or US lawful permanent residents intending to become citizens.
notes: Tuition awards do not stack with other USM tuition scholarships.

name: National Merit Scholarship (Tulane-sponsored)
value: At least $2,000 per year for Finalists who name Tulane first choice. If the NMSC award is one-year only, Tulane provides $2,000 per year thereafter while the student is a full-time Newcomb-Tulane undergraduate.
deadline: Name Tulane as first choice through the NMSC process.
apply: Be a National Merit Finalist and name Tulane as your first-choice school with NMSC.
eligibility: National Merit Finalists enrolling at Tulane. NMSC requires entrants to be US citizens or US lawful permanent residents intending to become citizens.
notes: The page does not name an entry year. Renewal follows NMSC requirements. Separate from Tulane's partial-tuition and full-tuition merit scholarships.

name: Chancellor's Merit Scholarship (National Merit Finalists)
value: Finalists who list Arkansas first: Chancellor's Merit Scholarship, $12,000 per year, with Honors College and priority benefits. Semifinalists are considered for the Chancellor's Scholarship ($10,000 per year) through the scholarship application.
deadline: List Arkansas first choice with NMSC by the required deadline (date not stated).
apply: Apply to Arkansas, upload your National Merit Finalist Certificate to the New Student Center, and confirm Arkansas as first choice with NMSC.
eligibility: National Merit Finalists (Semifinalists for the Chancellor's Scholarship) with a minimum 3.75 GPA. NMSC requires entrants to be US citizens or US lawful permanent residents intending to become citizens.
notes: The page does not name an entry year. Additional awards may be available by residency or major; Honors College fellowships need a separate application.

name: National Scholar awards (National Merit and National Recognition)
value: Arizona residents: National Merit Finalists $15,000 per year ($60,000 over four years); National Recognition awardees $10,000 per year ($40,000). Nonresidents: National Merit Finalists and National Recognition awardees $17,500 per year for eight semesters ($70,000).
deadline: National Merit Finalists select ASU first choice with NMSC by May 1. Nonresident awards require admission to and enrollment in Barrett, The Honors College (the page's Barrett date is March 15, 2026).
apply: National Merit Finalists: select ASU as first choice with NMSC by May 1. Nonresidents (both programs): be admitted to and enroll in Barrett, The Honors College.
eligibility: Incoming first-year National Merit Finalists and College Board National Recognition Program awardees. NMSC requires entrants to be US citizens or US lawful permanent residents intending to become citizens.
notes: Page dates are for the fall 2026 cycle. ASU also lists the Michelle Brown-Hollin Scholarship for out-of-state National Rural and Small Town Recognition awardees (3.25 GPA, Barrett admission).

name: National Distinction Scholarship
value: $40,000 total ($10,000 per year). Nonresident recipients may also qualify for the in-state tuition rate for the same period.
deadline: Select Texas State as first choice with NMSC on or before May 31 prior to your first semester.
apply: Be a National Merit Finalist or Semifinalist, submit an admission application and transcript, select Texas State first with NMSC by May 31, and email your certificate to processing@txstate.edu.
eligibility: First-time incoming freshmen who are National Merit Finalists or Semifinalists. NMSC requires entrants to be US citizens or US lawful permanent residents intending to become citizens.
notes: The page does not name an entry year. Renewal: 3.5 Texas State GPA and 28 passing hours per year.

name: National Hispanic Scholar award
value: An additional $4,000 per year on top of the LETU Merit Award, renewable with continuous full-time enrollment.
deadline: No deadline stated.
apply: Attend LeTourneau directly after high school and submit proof of your National Hispanic Recognition Program award.
eligibility: Students recognized in the College Board National Hispanic Recognition Program.
notes: The page does not name an entry year. Renewal requires a 2.0 cumulative GPA at the end of each spring.

name: Gold Scholar Award and National Merit University of Minnesota Scholarship
value: Gold Scholar Award for National Merit Finalists: amounts vary, up to $10,000 per year for four years. National Merit University of Minnesota Scholarship (college-sponsored): $2,000 per year for four years.
deadline: Declare UMN Twin Cities as first choice by the NMSC final deadline. Complete the admission application by November 1, December 1 or January 1 for full scholarship consideration.
apply: Apply for fall 2027 admission, become a National Merit Finalist, and declare UMN Twin Cities as first choice with NMSC by the final deadline.
eligibility: National Merit Finalists. The $2,000 scholarship is only for Finalists not eligible for an NMSC corporate-sponsored or National Merit $2500 Scholarship. NMSC requires entrants to be US citizens or US lawful permanent residents intending to become citizens.
notes: Gold Scholar preference is given to Finalists naming UMN first; amounts vary.

name: National Merit Scholarship
value: Full tuition scholarship, renewable for up to four years.
deadline: Choose UMN Morris as first choice with NMSC by the NMSC deadline.
apply: Be a National Merit Finalist and choose the University of Minnesota Morris as your first-choice college with NMSC.
eligibility: National Merit Finalists. NMSC requires entrants to be US citizens or US lawful permanent residents intending to become citizens.
notes: The page does not name an entry year.

name: UNT Meritorious Scholarship for National Merit Finalists
value: Covers tuition and mandatory fees, on-campus room and board (standard hall, double occupancy, 7-Day Basic meal plan) and textbooks. Four-year value: $108,000 in-state; $157,000 out-of-state.
deadline: Designate UNT with NMSC by NMSC's published deadline.
apply: Be a National Merit Finalist and designate UNT as your number one school with NMSC. FAFSA encouraged.
eligibility: National Merit Finalists. Non-Texas residents using the non-resident tuition waiver must meet Selective Service registration requirements. NMSC requires entrants to be US citizens or US lawful permanent residents intending to become citizens.
notes: The page does not name an entry year.

name: South Alabama Merit Scholarship (National Merit)
value: $2,000 per year, renewable for up to four years.
deadline: Be admitted by the priority admission deadline and apply in JagSPOT before the scholarship deadline. The page shows fall 2026 dates (priority February 15, 2026).
apply: Be an NMSC Finalist admitted by the priority admission deadline, inform NMSC that South Alabama is your first choice, and complete the JagSPOT application.
eligibility: NMSC Finalists admitted to South Alabama. NMSC requires entrants to be US citizens or US lawful permanent residents intending to become citizens.
notes: Page shows fall 2026 dates. Can be combined with a Freshman Admission Scholarship but not above the cost of attendance.

name: Jefferson Caffery Scholarship
value: 2027-2028: $4,000 ($500 per semester for 8 semesters) plus an estimated $4,000 for UL Lafayette study abroad.
deadline: All requirements must be met by February 1 of the graduating year.
apply: Be a National Merit Finalist or Semifinalist, be regularly admitted, and meet all requirements by February 1.
eligibility: National Merit Finalists or Semifinalists with a 3.0 cumulative unweighted GPA and 23 ACT or 1130 SAT; U.S. citizenship required.
notes: Not for online programs or Compete LA.

name: National Merit Scholarship
value: Full cost of attendance for four years (based on 30 credit hours per year).
